We look at the values at these indices:

- $ a(7) = 64 $
- $ a(15) = 448 = 7 \times 64 $
- $ a(23) = 1344 = 3 \times 448 $

This suggests a recurrence of the form:

$$
a(n) = k \cdot a(n - 8)
$$

where $ k $ is a multiplier that changes with each step. The multipliers are:

- $ 7 $ from $ a(7) $ to $ a(15) $
- $ 3 $ from $ a(15) $ to $ a(23) $

So, for $ n \equiv 7 \mod 8 $, we can define:

$$
a(n) = 
\begin{cases}
7 \cdot a(n - 8), & \text{if } n = 15 \\
3 \cdot a(n - 8), & \text{if } n = 23 \\
\end{cases}
$$

This implies the multiplier is decreasing by 4 each time.

From the above, we can generalize the recurrence as follows:

  $$

  $$
  where $ k $ is a decreasing sequence starting at 7.
